whatTheyArgued: Hubel & Wiesel (J. Physiol. 1959, cat striate cortex; 1962, cat visual cortex architecture; 1968, macaque) recorded single cortical neurons and showed each responds to light in a restricted region of the retina (its receptive field), with a preferred stimulus type (oriented bars, edges) and a classification into simple, complex and (in cat) hypercomplex cells, plus columnar organization by orientation and eye dominance. In the 1968 monkey paper (read from the journal PDF): receptive fields are smaller than in cat on average; the retinotopic map is coarser in the periphery but compensated by larger fields. Nothing in it concerns time, 'the present', or decay. The papers are copyrighted; manifest is copyrighted_deferred and nothing is quoted.

scholarship.ref: Hubel & Wiesel 1968, 'Receptive fields and functional architecture of monkey striate cortex', J. Physiol. 195:215-243 (read via pdftotext)
scholarship.supports: fields are local regions of retina; sizes vary with eccentricity and cell type; simple/complex/hypercomplex categories; columnar organization
scholarship.disputes: I did not read literature on extra-classical (surround/contextual) influences on cortical responses, so I cannot say here whether 'responds only to a bounded region' is too strong; flagged unverified

ourUse: terrain-activation.js lights the terrains a proposition touches across the nine-cell grid (Entity, Link, Network, Field, Void, Lens), fades everything at the reader's own gamma (measured by dmdWindow), so per-proposition cost is O(what it touches). Handle comment: 'the reach of the present moment is local and bounded, like a cortical neuron's patch of the visual field'.

bends.ours: 'Reach of the present': a time-decaying set of lit graph terrains for one reader.
bends.theirs: A receptive field is a spatial region of the retina for one neuron; Hubel & Wiesel's papers do not treat time-decay or a reader's present.

bends.ours: Bound is a decay window we measure or declare (gamma, dmdWindow), with a null arm (gamma null) in which nothing fades.
bends.theirs: Field extent is a measured property of each cell that varies by cell type and eccentricity; there is no single bound, and no undecayed control.

bends.ours: credit line: 'a neuron's reach is local and bounded: the present never spans the whole field.' The second clause is our design rule written as if part of their finding; the work line also says 'activation never spans the whole'.
bends.theirs: They did not claim anything about 'the present' or about whole-field activation being excluded; many cells together do cover the whole field (the retinotopic map).
Wiesel shared the 1981 Nobel and co-authored every cited paper; the manifest giver is Hubel only.
